title: Read a paper without overselling it
goal: Separate research question, method, result and real-world applicability.
explanation: A paper’s abstract is not enough to establish a practical business benefit. Check the population, sample, comparison, outcome and stated limitations. Use the original fictional abstract first; when trying an actual paper, access a legitimate copy and keep its title/version. AI summaries are reading aids, not peer review.
sampleInput: Fictional abstract: “Twenty volunteers were randomly assigned to checklist or no-checklist groups for a simulated packing task. Median omissions were 1 versus 3. The task lasted one afternoon. No long-term retention, business revenue or safety outcome was measured.”
prompt: Explain the question, sample, comparison, measured outcome and limitations in plain language. Separate the reported result from three possible follow-up applications, each labelled a hypothesis. Do not invent statistical significance, causal mechanisms, long-term effects or revenue gains.
workedExample: Reported: lower median omissions in the checklist group in this small simulated task. Hypothesis: test a checklist in a different packing workflow. Unsupported: “checklists triple business productivity” or “the study proves permanent safety improvements.”

steps.title: Read the supplied abstract
steps.text: Highlight population, comparison, outcome, duration and limitations.

steps.title: Generate a structured summary
steps.text: Ask for separate method, result and applicability sections.

steps.title: Check each claim
steps.text: Trace the summary to exact abstract words; mark missing statistics as missing.

steps.title: Design a follow-up
steps.text: Choose one setting and define a measurable outcome plus a risk/limitation.

steps.title: Try a real paper optionally
steps.text: Read methods and limitations, not just the generated summary, before proposing any application.

checks: Sample size, simulated context and one-afternoon duration remain visible.
No significance level, revenue result or long-term benefit is invented.
Suggested applications are hypotheses with a proposed test, not established findings.
commonMistakes: Turning a small simulated result into a universal business claim.
Accepting citations or statistics that do not occur in the paper.
offline: Complete the question/method/result/limit table by hand from the fictional abstract.
reflection: Which business use would require the biggest leap beyond the reported evidence?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Sample size, simulated context and one-afternoon duration remain visible.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. No significance level, revenue result or long-term benefit is invented.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Turning a small simulated result into a universal business claim.
